automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector
collector_scope: Raw-only public-source collection for AI-assisted development practice updates. No docs/wiki pages or raw/processed files were updated.

cutoff_window.date_rule: Include only sources with a direct visible publication or update date within the last 2 days relative to the run timestamp. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

federation_boundary.local_scope: Practice-level implications for AI-assisted development workflows, governance, verification, context, adoption, permissions, auditability, and operating model.
federation_boundary.handling_rule: For upstream-owned entities, record the entity as upstream-owned and keep only the downstream practice implication or routing note.

qualifying_updates.title: Repository metadata suggestions become a governance assist
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced a public preview where Copilot suggests allowed values while enterprise or organization owners create repository custom property definitions. Custom properties can attach governance metadata to repositories and target rulesets; the feature includes a policy control for repository custom property suggestions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI-assisted development governance depends on repository metadata that is consistent enough to drive rules, review requirements, and security policies. Suggested values move part of taxonomy creation into the admin workflow, while still requiring organization owners to decide whether suggestions fit local governance language.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat generated repository metadata suggestions as a starting point for governed taxonomy design, not as authority; keep human-owned policy language and review before applying rulesets across repository fleets.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: If ingested, route product details upstream and keep the downstream lens on metadata taxonomies for repository policy targeting.

qualifying_updates.title: Enterprise security configurations gain stronger enforcement
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced that enterprise administrators can enforce GitHub Advanced Security configurations across organizations, preventing organization and repository administrators from overriding enterprise-level settings. The changelog describes enforcement levels for repository owners or both repository and organization owners.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent-generated changes increase the need for centrally enforced security gates that local repositories cannot silently weaken. The update is practice evidence for separating enterprise security baselines from team-level convenience settings.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Record that AI-assisted repositories may need non-overridable security configuration baselines for scanning, secret blocking, and review gates when code generation increases change volume.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use as local governance evidence; avoid duplicating GitHub product coverage.

qualifying_updates.title: AI coding-agent onboarding guidance emphasizes selective context
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Improving published guidance that AI coding agents need onboarding through coding standards, architecture patterns, ADRs, and context files. The article distinguishes context from guardrails and warns against dumping all documentation into context because stale or excessive material can increase cost and reproduce obsolete patterns.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The article reinforces durable local practices already relevant to this wiki: agents need concise, high-signal instructions, rationale-bearing ADRs, structured context files, and deterministic guardrails rather than broad documentation dumps.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Context files should prioritize current standards, architectural rationale, and business vocabulary while moving enforceable requirements into deterministic checks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Good candidate evidence for durable instructions, context selection, and guardrail boundary pages.

qualifying_updates.title: Agentic PR queues require evidence-based triage
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: CodeRabbit described a triage layer for pull-request queues where agent-created work can arrive faster than teams can review it. The post argues that review queues need priority, risk, ownership, effort, blocker, dependency, and evidence signals before a reviewer opens a PR, and that human judgment remains necessary for architectural and product decisions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is practice-level evidence that the bottleneck in agentic software delivery shifts from code generation to deciding which generated changes deserve human attention and which review depth is appropriate.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local review workflows should model review capacity as a scarce resource and require visible evidence for priority, risk, reviewer assignment, and next action before accepting agent-generated PR volume.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: If ingested, anchor the product upstream and keep the local page focused on PR triage and review-capacity governance.

qualifying_updates.title: Deployment error diagnosis becomes an agent handoff artifact
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Mastra announced deployment error diagnosis in its platform and CLI. Failed deploys can be inspected by deploy ID, project, or environment; user errors receive explanations and recommendations that highlight problem code, and users can copy a Markdown diagnosis summary for a coding agent or downstream service.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The update shows a concrete handoff pattern: runtime/build failures are summarized into structured, copyable evidence for an agent repair loop while raw logs remain available for inspection.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Repair loops should preserve machine-readable or Markdown evidence packages that summarize the failure, classify ownership, point to problem code, and retain access to raw logs for verifier review.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Useful for pages about regression repair, runtime telemetry, and agent handoffs.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent observability adds request-level server health
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Mastra announced a server-health request view for deployed Mastra servers. The view captures traffic, average and p95 duration, status over time, latency percentiles, high-traffic endpoints, and separates views by environment such as production and staging.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent applications need ordinary production observability, not only model traces. Request-level health data gives teams a way to validate that agent services remain performant and reliable after prompt, tool, or deployment changes.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Production agent harnesses should include request-level service health, environment separation, latency/error tracking, and endpoint-level visibility alongside model/tool traces.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Pair with user-visible progress and runtime telemetry or agent harness observability pages if ingested.

qualifying_updates.title: Grab LLM-Kit analysis highlights shared agent plumbing
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: InfoQ analyzed Grab's LLM-Kit, an internal framework reportedly standardizing more than 500 internal agent services. The analysis emphasizes shared scaffolding for agent loops, evaluation, tracing, secret handling, MCP tool-server connections, model gateway access, and production service templates, with the original Grab post noting that production wrapping once took far longer than the reasoning loop.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The article is strong practice evidence that agent platform work concentrates in shared infrastructure: secrets, tracing, service discovery, eval endpoints, model gateways, remote tool discovery, and templates that prevent every team from solving the same safety and deployment problems.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: A durable local lens could describe agent platform templates as the way teams centralize non-negotiable plumbing while preserving local agent implementation ownership.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Original Grab source is July 24, 2026 and outside this collector window; use the September 15 InfoQ analysis as the qualifying source and the Grab post as context only during ingest.

qualifying_updates.title: Automated RCA models telemetry correlation as evidence ranking
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: InfoQ reported on Atlassian's automated root-cause analysis approach, which correlates metrics, logs, distributed traces, and service topology. The system detects anomalies, aligns them on a common timeline, maps them through a service dependency graph, and returns ranked hypotheses with supporting evidence.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Even when not specific to coding agents, the pattern is directly useful for agent repair workflows: agents should receive ranked hypotheses grounded in telemetry evidence rather than isolated log snippets.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Agent repair and incident-response workflows should package telemetry as ranked, evidence-backed hypotheses across metrics, logs, traces, and topology rather than relying on single-signal context.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: If ingested, keep this as a workflow/evidence pattern, not broad Atlassian or observability-product coverage.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent authentication comparison separates delegate and principal models
qualifying_updates.visible_date: September 14, 2026 table date; related resource shown September 15, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: AgentMail compared AI agent authentication platforms as of September 14, 2026. The article distinguishes delegated access, workload identity, registration protocols, and agent identity providers; it also contrasts agents acting as delegates for users with agents acting as principals with their own account identity and accountable human metadata.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent tool access and MCP authorization increasingly depend on a clear identity model. The article is useful practice evidence for choosing whether a coding or workflow agent should borrow a user's authority, run as a workload identity, or authenticate as its own accountable principal.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local governance should distinguish delegated user authority, workload identity, registration flow, and portable agent principal identity before granting tools, issuing tokens, or auditing agent actions.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Disclosure says AgentID is built by AgentMail; use as taxonomy evidence and verify vendor-specific status before durable product claims.

qualifying_updates.title: Multi-agent technical-debt audits frame specialized review roles
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Syncfusion described using multi-agent AI systems for technical-debt detection and management. The article presents specialized analysis across architecture, security, performance, testing, and code quality, and frames repository-wide audits as a way to identify risks and prioritize improvements rather than relying only on periodic review.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The article supports the local practice of separating reviewer roles by concern area and using repository-wide audits to decide which generated or accumulated changes need attention.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Repository-health review loops can assign specialized agent or reviewer roles for architecture, security, performance, testing, and code-quality concerns, while keeping prioritization and acceptance accountable to humans.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Community/vendor source; use for practice framing, not as independent validation of product capability.
